title: Hugging Face releases ToyBlocks simulation framework for robot learning
excerpt: The framework provides a controlled environment for researchers to study robot behavior and train models using simulated tabletop tasks.
bodyHtml:
Hugging Face announced the release of ToyBlocks on November 6, 2026. The framework is designed as a FoundationWorld, which pairs a simulated environment with tools for generating tasks, training demonstrations, and measuring robot performance.

ToyBlocks features a robot arm and blocks on a tabletop, requiring the robot to reason about interactions while pushing, flipping, and stacking objects. The framework uses reinforcement learning and motion planning to generate skills for short-horizon tasks within the Isaac Lab simulation environment.

Researchers can use ToyBlocks to study how models generalize to new tasks, evaluate spatial reasoning, and test high-level planning. The system can generate and execute hundreds of plans in parallel on a single graphics processing unit, reaching up to 24 times real-time performance.

The framework also includes a webpage interface that lets users connect Claude or another frontier model to instruct the robot using natural language. Hugging Face plans to extend this approach to increasingly complex environments in the future.
topic: ToyBlocks: A controlled world for robot learning and evaluation
